"Let $\mathbb{P}$ be a partial field, and let $\mathbb{L}\mathbb{P}$ denote its lift. **Lift idempotence conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{L}^2\mathbb{P} \cong \mathbb{L}\mathbb{P}.
$$

The conjecture is related to whether the canonical homomorphism from the lift back to the original partial field induces a bijection on fundamental elements. The paper gives no resolution."

statement_tokens.token: "Let $x,y,z\\in X$ be three wells in a graph with equal pairwise distances $a=b=c$, and let $c_{uv}$ denote the sum over shortest paths from $u$ to $v$ of the products of inverse square roots of the degrees of consecutive vertices. Assume $c_{xy}=c_{xz}\\neq c_{yz}$. **Perfect tunneling conjecture.** There is always perfect tunneling from $y$ to $z$. This conjecture concerns the remaining asymmetric case of the equilateral triple-well setup, after distinguishing whether the relevant quantity $\\sqrt{c_{yz}^2+8c_{xz}^2}$ is rational or irrational; the stated theorem gives different tunneling-time behavior in those cases, but does not resolve this assertion."

statement_tokens.token:
"Let $H$ be a connected spanning subgraph of a nontrivial connected graph $G$, and let $src(G)$ denote the strong rainbow connection number of $G$. **Chartrand's conjecture.** One has

$$
src(G)\leq src(H).
$$

Unlike ordinary rainbow connection number, strong rainbow connection number is not generally monotone under adding edges, so this proposed inequality is a natural but nontrivial strengthening of the known result under the additional hypothesis $diam(H)=2$."
